scenes.line1: How do systems run lots of tasks fast?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how servers handle tons of tasks at once without slowing down? What's the trick behind their speed?

scenes.label: ThreadPool
scenes.sub: Manages reusable threads for efficient task execution.
scenes.say: A thread pool keeps a bunch of threads ready to work, so you don’t waste time creating new ones for every single task.
Executors handle the thread setup. Tasks go into a work queue, and worker threads pull jobs from there to run. It’s all automated.

scenes.code:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
    executor.submit(my_task)
scenes.say: In Python, you can use a thread pool executor to run tasks. This lets you control how many threads are working at once.

scenes.question: Why not create a new thread for each task?
scenes.wrong: Threads are cheap, so it's fine.
scenes.right: Creating threads is expensive. Pools reuse threads, saving resources and boosting performance.
scenes.say: Interviewers love to ask why you shouldn’t just make a new thread for every job. Remember, thread pools avoid the overhead and keep things efficient.
